---
title: "Bound the work of a match"
description: >
  Set match, depth and heap limits so that a pattern or input you do not
  trust gives an error or an NA instead of a stall.
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

This guide is for code that matches patterns or strings it did not write:
a pattern typed by a user, lines from a file someone uploaded. It shows
how a match can take very long, how `re_limits()` stops it, and what the
limits do not promise.

```{r setup}
library(zuregex)
```

## The problem

PCRE2 matches by backtracking: when one way of matching fails, it goes
back and tries the next. A pattern with a repeat inside a repeat, such as
`^(a+)+$`, has a number of ways that doubles with each extra `a`, and a
subject that almost matches makes PCRE2 try them all. Twenty `a`s and a
`!` still get an answer. Thirty do not: the search runs into PCRE2's own
limit of ten million steps, and the call fails.

```{r, error = TRUE}
subject <- function(n) paste0(strrep("a", n), "!")
re_detect(subject(20), "^(a+)+$")
re_detect(subject(30), "^(a+)+$")
```

So a match cannot run for ever. But ten million steps is a lot of work to
spend on each bad string in a long vector, and the error loses the
answers for the good ones.

## Set a limit for a call

Every matching function takes `limits`, made by `re_limits()`. `match`
is the number of steps one search may take. Here it is ten thousand, a
thousandth of the default. The error has the class `zuregex_error_limit`,
so you can tell it from a pattern that does not compile, and handle it.

```{r}
x <- c(subject(30), "aaa")
tryCatch(
  re_detect(x, "^(a+)+$", limits = re_limits(match = 1e4)),
  zuregex_error_limit = function(e) "too much work"
)
```

## Keep the elements that finished

One bad string should not always lose the whole vector. With
`on_limit = "na"`, an element that hits a limit is `NA`, the others are
matched as usual, and the call gives one warning that counts the `NA`s.
The second element here is `TRUE`.

```{r}
re_detect(x, "^(a+)+$", limits = re_limits(match = 1e4, on_limit = "na"))
```

The warning has the class `zuregex_warning_limit`.

## Set a limit for the session

The option `zuregex.limits` applies to every call that does not pass
`limits` itself. Printing the object shows what it holds.

```{r}
old <- options(zuregex.limits = re_limits(match = 1e5, on_limit = "na"))
getOption("zuregex.limits")
options(old)
```

## What the limits do not promise

* **Not linear time.** A limit bounds the work for each element; it does
  not make the pattern cheap. For a guarantee that matching time grows
  only with the length of the input, use the
  [re2](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=re2) package.
* **Not a time in seconds.** `match` counts PCRE2's steps, which differ
  in cost from pattern to pattern. Choose it by trying your real
  patterns.
* **Not compiling.** The limits bound matching. Compiling is bounded
  separately: a compiled pattern may take at most 16 MiB, which
  `re_compile_size()` changes.
* **`depth` and `heap` bind only the interpreter.** PCRE2's just-in-time
  compiler honours `match` and ignores the other two, so `match` is the
  limit to rely on.

## See also

`?re_limits` describes each limit and PCRE2's defaults. The C API has the
same limits; see
[Link to zuregex from C](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuregex/articles/c-api.html).
